script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for June 23. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Look at a tile floor or honeycomb: shapes fitting together with no gaps, no overlaps.  This is tessellation—and only certain shapes can do it.  Nature discovered this for beehives; mathematicians proved which shapes work and why.

At every meeting point, angles must total exactly 360 degrees—a full rotation. Squares: 4 × 90° = 360°. Triangles: 6 × 60° = 360°. Hexagons: 3 × 120° = 360°. Pentagons: 108° × 3 = 324°. Doesn't work. Bees build hexagonal cells because hexagons are the most efficient tessellating shape—enclosing the most area with the least perimeter.  Minimum wax, maximum honey storage.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Fitting together is a design problem.  Tessellation teaches that the right pieces interlock perfectly; the wrong pieces always leave gaps.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Fit Check - What Interlocks in Your Life?.

Here's your activity: Consider the elements of your life—work, relationships, hobbies, rest. Do they tessellate (fit together smoothly) or leave gaps and overlaps? What adjustments would help everything interlock better? Good design means pieces that fit. This helps you evaluate how elements fit together.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about shapes that tile perfectly can be applied to fit check - what interlocks in your life?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
